item.text:
<linkedin_post>Extension auto-updates can bring a compromised package onto a developer’s machine without a new installation decision. In the Claude Code incident, a tampered update appeared under Anthropic’s legitimate extension ID in Cursor’s marketplace.

The malicious code attempted to add an attacker-controlled SSH key, set up persistence and establish a reverse tunnel. Whether an attacker could log in depended on the host’s permissions and SSH configuration. The code could still write a key, install persistence and send host details when that access failed.

Cursor’s revised advisory identifies versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 distributed through its marketplace for Windows and macOS. Organizations investigating exposure should check update records as well as installations, then isolate affected hosts and preserve evidence. Removing the extension leaves any artifacts written outside its directory to be dealt with separately.</linkedin_post>
